samples.claim_zh: 该研究通过空间转录组技术和细胞谱系追踪，首次揭示了黄瓜下位子房的发育机制，并阐明了KNOX1转录因子在葫芦科植物花器官发育和性别决定中的核心作用。

classify_evidences.text: Genetic knockout of a receptacle-specific KNOX1 transcription factor in cucumber caused arrest in receptacle growth and yielded bisexual flowers with superior ovaries similar to those of tomato.
Here we provide developmental and mechanistic insights into inferior ovary formation and sex determination in cucurbits.

Comparative spatial transcriptome mapping and cell lineage reconstructions in developing floral buds of cucumber and tomato, which have inferior and superior ovaries, respectively, revealed that inferior ovaries develop from accelerated receptacle growth resulting from the continuous activity of meristematic stems cells at the base of the cucumber floral organs.

The mutation of just KNAT2-like1 in cucumber simultaneously leads to the formation of bisexual flowers and superior ovaries, suggesting that during receptacle evolution a direct link was established between the development of the unisexual flowers and inferior ovaries.
Theses findings provide genetic evidence that both the promotion of the receptacle formation and the suppression of stamen development are orchestrated by a single KNOX1 TF.

classify_evidences.text: Based on these observations, we inferred three necessary conditions for the formation of the inferior ovary in cucumber: (1) enlargement of the floral meristem to change the relative position of the floral whorls, (2) subsequent rapid growth of the receptacle and (3) fusion of the receptacle and the carpel.

Comparative spatial transcriptome mapping and cell lineage reconstructions in developing floral buds of cucumber and tomato, which have inferior and superior ovaries, respectively, revealed that inferior ovaries develop from accelerated receptacle growth resulting from the continuous activity of meristematic stems cells at the base of the cucumber floral organs.

With the rapid growth of the receptacle, the sepal, petal and stamen primordia are elevated to the floral apex, while the carpel remains inside the receptacle, thereby forming inferior ovaries (Fig. 1b,c).
In female flowers, the receptacle and carpel continued to grow after S5, and the receptacle grew rapidly and wrapped around the carpel to form the inferior ovary (Extended Data Fig. 7b,d).

The formation of male floral buds in cucumber, induced by AgNO3, also featured an enlarged and concave floral meristem; however, the subsequent growth of the receptacle and carpel was arrested (Extended Data Fig. 1c).

classify_evidences.text: In this current study, we generated a comprehensive collection of spatially resolved transcriptomes and reconstructed the cellular territories and cell lineages for the continuously developing floral organs of cucumber.

Comparative spatial transcriptome mapping and cell lineage reconstructions in developing floral buds of cucumber and tomato, which have inferior and superior ovaries, respectively, revealed that inferior ovaries develop from accelerated receptacle growth resulting from the continuous activity of meristematic stems cells at the base of the cucumber floral organs.

The data related to these spatially and temporally resolved transcriptomes and cell types of cucumber floral organ development can be browsed via the STOmicsDB27, an interactive data portal, at https://db.cngb.org/ stomics/ctsta.

Our findings revealed that the prolonged activity of the FIM at the base of the floral organs is responsible for the initiation and rapid growth of the receptacle, leading to female flower determination and the formation of an inferior ovary.
However, the developmental mechanisms underlying inferior ovary formation remain largely unknown.

classify_evidences.text: In this current study, we generated a comprehensive collection of spatially resolved transcriptomes and reconstructed the cellular territories and cell lineages for the continuously developing floral organs of cucumber.

Our findings revealed that the prolonged activity of the FIM at the base of the floral organs is responsible for the initiation and rapid growth of the receptacle, leading to female flower determination and the formation of an inferior ovary.

Comparative spatial transcriptome mapping and cell lineage reconstructions in developing floral buds of cucumber and tomato, which have inferior and superior ovaries, respectively, revealed that inferior ovaries develop from accelerated receptacle growth resulting from the continuous activity of meristematic stems cells at the base of the cucumber floral organs.
However, the developmental mechanisms underlying inferior ovary formation remain largely unknown.
Genetic knockout of a receptacle-specific KNOX1 transcription factor in cucumber caused arrest in receptacle growth and yielded bisexual flowers with superior ovaries similar to those of tomato.

To dissect the underlying gene expression network driving the development of the inferior ovary of cucumber, we sampled floral buds at various stages, including S1–S8, and ovaries at 0 days post anthesis (DPA) for spatial transcriptomic analysis.

Comparative spatial transcriptome mapping and cell lineage reconstructions in developing floral buds of cucumber and tomato, which have inferior and superior ovaries, respectively, revealed that inferior ovaries develop from accelerated receptacle growth resulting from the continuous activity of meristematic stems cells at the base of the cucumber floral organs.
In total, seven clusters were identified for both the superior ovary mutant and tomato.

The mutation of just KNAT2-like1 in cucumber simultaneously leads to the formation of bisexual flowers and superior ovaries, suggesting that during receptacle evolution a direct link was established between the development of the unisexual flowers and inferior ovaries.
